# Tether calibration for 'Robot log: first day on the real bench' (Robot manipulation, 20 runs, 2026-10-10)
# NVIDIA Newton: XPBD averages the two materials' mu, so set both to the measured pair value.
import newton

MU_EFF = 0.7006  # box-table sliding friction, 90% interval 0.6912 - 0.7077 (bootstrap)
object_cfg = newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=MU_EFF)
surface_cfg = newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=MU_EFF)
# builder.add_shape_box(body, hx=..., hy=..., hz=..., cfg=object_cfg)   # the box
# builder.add_ground_plane(cfg=surface_cfg)                             # the table

ACTUATOR_GAIN = 0.8749  # arm strength: actual speed / commanded (0.8643 - 0.8847); scale commanded velocities

# Measured friction region (spill, mat, worn spot) along the travel axis (+y from the launch point).
FRICTION_REGION = {'y_start_m': 0.3765, 'mu_eff': 0.4527}  # y 0.368-0.385, mu 0.439-0.461
# Two surface bodies leave a seam that trips sliding objects; Tether instead switches the object's own mu
# when it crosses y_start with a Warp kernel and ground mu 0 (see sim/newton_push.py: _patch_setup).

# Perception (line distance as the robot camera reports it):
CAMERA = {'dx_m': -0.0004, 'pitch_error_deg': 2.288, 'lens_k_per_m': -0.00910}
# perceived = true * (1 + tan(pitch)) + dx + lens_k * true**2
exports.isaaclab:
"""Tether calibrated domain randomization for 'Robot log: first day on the real bench' (2026-10-10).
Ranges are 90% bootstrap intervals of the measured values, not hand-picked bounds: train on what the real
table can plausibly be, nothing wider. PhysX "average" friction combine (the default) matches the measurement."""
from isaaclab.envs import mdp
from isaaclab.managers import EventTermCfg as EventTerm
from isaaclab.managers import SceneEntityCfg
from isaaclab.utils import configclass


@configclass
class CalibratedEventCfg:
    # sliding friction of the box-table pair; static friction is not observed by a sliding test
    object_material = EventTerm(
        func=mdp.randomize_rigid_body_material,
        mode="startup",
        params={
            "asset_cfg": SceneEntityCfg("object"),
            "static_friction_range": (0.6912, 0.7077),
            "dynamic_friction_range": (0.6912, 0.7077),
            "restitution_range": (0.0, 0.0),
            "num_buckets": 64,
            "make_consistent": True,
        },
    )


# Arm strength: the real launch speed is 0.875x the command (90% 0.864-0.885). It belongs
# in the push action's scale (joint names: your robot's).
ACTUATOR_GAIN = 0.8749
push_action = mdp.JointVelocityActionCfg(asset_name="robot", joint_names=[".*"], scale=ACTUATOR_GAIN)


# Friction region (spill, mat, worn spot): from y = 0.377 m (90% 0.368-0.385) the pair slides at mu 0.453
# (90% 0.439-0.461). A static table prim whose top is flush with the first;
# shorten the first one so it ends at REGION_Y0 (overlapping coplanar surfaces leave PhysX two materials to pick from).
# Its combine mode 'min' outranks PhysX's default 'average', so the pair takes the region's value.
import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils
from isaaclab.assets import AssetBaseCfg

REGION_Y0 = 0.3765  # m along the push axis from the launch point
SURFACE_TOP_Z = 0.0  # set to your table top height
calibrated_region = AssetBaseCfg(
    prim_path="{ENV_REGEX_NS}/CalibratedRegion",
    spawn=sim_utils.CuboidCfg(
        size=(0.4, 2.0, 0.002),  # across the path, along it from REGION_Y0, thin
        collision_props=sim_utils.CollisionPropertiesCfg(),
        physics_material=sim_utils.RigidBodyMaterialCfg(static_friction=0.4527, dynamic_friction=0.4527,
                                                        friction_combine_mode="min"),
    ),
    init_state=AssetBaseCfg.InitialStateCfg(pos=(0.0, REGION_Y0 + 1.0, SURFACE_TOP_Z - 0.001)),
)
exports.markdown:
# Sim2Real calibration: Robot log: first day on the real bench

Domain: **Robot manipulation**. A robot arm pushes a box so it stops on a line. The table may be slicker, wet in places, or the arm weaker than in simulation.

20 runs (log), structure chosen by Nemotron agent (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b). Stop residual 0 cm rms.

## What differs from your simulator

| Parameter | Sim | Real (measured) | 90% interval | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Box-table friction | 0.800 | 0.701 | 0.691 – 0.708 | changed |
| Arm strength (actual / commanded speed) | 1.000x | 0.875x | 0.864x – 0.885x | changed |
| Friction region starts at | none | 0.377 m | 0.368 m – 0.385 m | changed |
| Friction in that region | none | 0.453 | 0.439 – 0.461 | changed |
| Camera offset | 0.000 m | -0.000 m | -0.008 m – 0.016 m | within noise |
| Camera tilt error | 0.000 deg | 2.288 deg | -3.119 deg – 4.764 deg | within noise |
| Lens distortion | 0.000 1/m | -0.009 1/m | -0.064 1/m – 0.118 1/m | within noise |

## Predicted effect (model rollouts, not measured)

Success = stopping within 3 cm of the line, over targets 0.2 m–0.6 m, for a policy trained in each simulator:

- current sim: **66%** (90%: 56–78%)
- calibrated sim: **100%** (90%: 100–100%)

## Next experiment

- run so the box stops near **0.63 m** (command 3.12): models disagree by ±0.8 cm here
- run so the box stops near **0.54 m** (command 2.94): models disagree by ±0.7 cm here
- run so the box stops near **0.45 m** (command 2.76): models disagree by ±0.7 cm here

## Agent's explanation

> Added a friction patch starting at 0.38 m with higher friction to capture position‑dependent deceleration; adjusted actuator gain to 0.87; camera pitch ~2.3° and slight lens distortion fix perception bias.

Generated by Tether Studio (NVIDIA Newton physics, Nemotron agent). Intervals: bootstrap over runs.
